_meta.note: Close a real plugin/Python divergence the how-to work surfaced: `hb exec config` prints the resolved executor config in the plugin (hb-exec.js), but the Python CLI declares exec's `action` arg and never reads it — so `hb exec config` there RUNS the executor instead of printing config. Fix: the Python exec handler honors action == 'config' (print executor.config as JSON) and 'run' (default), rejecting anything else. Spec-first: a failing pytest first. This is behavioral parity (both runtimes have `exec config` that prints and does not run) — NOT byte-equal output: the key format differs by design (plugin camelCase attemptCap/heartbeatMs, Python snake_case attempt_cap/heartbeat_s), so config stays out of the byte-equal parity.sh surface and is recorded as an intentional divergence in parity-notes. EC0: the fix + pytest. WR0: restore the choose-a-backend doc line (now true), note the intentional divergence in parity-notes, and add a T63 node-suite group asserting both runtimes' `exec config` print a backend and Python's does not run. Suites stay green.

tasks.description: In py/src/heartbeat/cli.py, make the exec handler honor args.action: 'config' -> print json.dumps(executor.config(hb), indent=2) and return 0; 'run' (default) -> existing behavior (respecting --parallel); anything else -> usage error to stderr, return 2. Mirrors the plugin's `hb-exec.js config`. Keep the Python and Node suites green.

In planning/parity-notes.md, record `exec config` as a shared command with intentionally runtime-specific key format (plugin camelCase vs Python snake_case) — a deliberate divergence, so it is not on the byte-equal parity surface. Keep prose-check green on the doc.
